questions.q: What does the Create Accounting process do?
options: It defines the chart of accounts for the first time
It applies accounting rules against unaccounted transactions and generates journal entries
It issues payments to suppliers
It matches invoices to purchase orders
questions.explain: Create Accounting runs the configured accounting rules against outstanding transactions to produce journal entries.

questions.q: What is the main benefit of running Create Accounting in Draft mode first?
options: It pays all outstanding invoices immediately
It deletes incorrect invoices automatically
It lets you preview and catch errors before anything posts permanently
It is required before any invoice can be validated
questions.explain: Draft mode generates entries for review without posting them permanently, which is useful for catching setup problems first.

questions.q: In the Harbor Point Logistics example, what caused one invoice to error out during the Draft run?
options: Its expense account combination didn't exist in the chart of accounts
The invoice amount was negative
The supplier had no bank account on file
The invoice was missing a purchase order
questions.explain: The error was an invalid account combination -- a setup issue, not a transactional one.

questions.q: What typically controls the accounting date assigned to an entry?
options: It is always the date the supplier was created
The date the purchase order was approved
A random date chosen by Create Accounting
Payables accounting options, which can use the invoice date, system date, or goods received date
questions.explain: Payables accounting options determine which date basis (invoice, system, or receipt date) is used for the accounting date.

questions.q: What happens to a transaction that errors out during Create Accounting?
options: The entire batch of transactions fails and nothing is accounted
It is skipped and remains unaccounted until the underlying issue is fixed and the process reruns
It is automatically deleted from the system
It posts anyway with a zero-dollar amount
questions.explain: An erroring transaction doesn't block the rest of the batch -- it's reported and stays unaccounted until corrected.
